metadata.title: Chicken Nuggets with Blackberry Mustard
metadata.description:
INGREDIENTS
1 cup fresh blackberries chopped
1 1/2 tablespoons whole-grain mustard
2 teaspoons honey
1 pound chicken tenders, cut in half crosswise
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground pepper
3 tablespoons cornmeal
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil

Directions: 
Mash blackberries (or raspberries), mustard and honey in a small bowl until it looks like a chunky sauce.

Sprinkle chicken tenders with salt and pepper. Place cornmeal in a medium bowl, add the chicken and toss to coat (discard any leftover cornmeal).

Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium and cook the chicken, turning once or twice, until browned and just cooked through, 6 to 8 minutes total (thinner nuggets will cook faster than thicker ones). Serve the chicken nuggets with the berry mustard.

You can also bake these in the oven instead if you want, but using a pan helps make them more crispy. 

Macros: 185 calories, 26 protein, 9 carbs, 5 fat

Macros w/broccoli and potato: 421 calories, 33 protein, 63 carb, 5 fat.

Originally uploaded Sept 5th, 2011. 

Shirts: http://campbellfitness.spreadshirt.com/

Facebook: http://www.facebook.com/CampbellFitness

Twitter: http://www.twitter.com/campbellfitness

summary.brief: Brandon seasons, breads, and pan‑fries chicken nuggets, prepares a blackberry‑mustard sauce, and plates the nuggets with broccoli and sweet potatoes.
summary.detailed: The video opens with Brandon greeting the audience in his kitchen and displaying all of the ingredients: chicken tenders, cornmeal, salt, pepper, olive oil, broccoli, sweet potatoes, blackberries, whole‑grain mustard, and honey. He seasons the chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then tosses each piece in a bowl of cornmeal to give a light coating and arranges the coated nuggets on a baking sheet. He heats a skillet with a little olive oil, adds the nuggets, watches them brown, and flips them after a few minutes, cooking them for a total of six to eight minutes. While the chicken cooks, he steams the broccoli and bakes the sweet potatoes in the oven. He then mixes a cup of chopped blackberries, about a tablespoon and a half of whole‑grain mustard, and two teaspoons of honey in a bowl, mashing them together into a chunky sauce. Once the nuggets are done, he plates the chicken beside the steamed broccoli and baked sweet potatoes, drizzles the blackberry‑mustard sauce over the top, and displays the final dish along with nutrition information before the video ends with the Campbell Fitness logo.

Additionally, the person may be preparing a special dish that requires the use of aluminum foil, such as a meatloaf, turkey, chicken, and fish fillets. The foil may protect the pan from drips while cooking, and the foil contains the mess of the food that would otherwise spill out of the baking pan. summary_sent_to_llm.title: Chicken Nuggets with Blackberry Mustard
summary_sent_to_llm.description:
INGREDIENTS
1 cup fresh blackberries chopped
1 1/2 tablespoons whole-grain mustard
2 teaspoons honey
1 pound chicken tenders, cut in half crosswise
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground pepper
3 tablespoons cornmeal
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil

Directions: 
Mash blackberries (or raspberries), mustard and honey in a small bowl until it looks like a chunky sauce.

Sprinkle chicken tenders with salt and pepper. Place cornmeal in a medium bowl, add the chicken and toss to coat (discard any leftover cornmeal).

Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Reduce heat
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with Brandon greeting the audience in his kitchen and displaying all of the ingredients: chicken tenders, cornmeal, salt, pepper, olive oil, broccoli, sweet potatoes, blackberries, whole‑grain mustard, and honey. He seasons the chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then tosses each piece in a bowl of cornmeal to give a light coating and arranges the coated nuggets on a baking sheet. He heats a skillet with a little olive oil, adds the nuggets, watches them brown, and flips them after a few minutes, cooking them for a total of six to eight minutes. While the chicken cooks, he steams the broccoli and bakes the sweet potatoes in the oven. He then mixes a cup of chopped blackberries, about a tablespoon and a half of whole‑grain mustard, and two teaspoons of honey in a bowl, mashing them together into a chunky sauce. Once the nuggets are done, he plates the chicken beside the steamed broccoli and baked sweet potatoes, drizzles the blackberry‑mustard sauce over the top, and displays the final dish along with nutrition information before the video ends with the Campbell Fitness logo.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
